turns.response_html:
That is a Gua Sha tool (specifically a stainless steel version from Kitsch). Originally used in traditional Chinese medicine, it’s now a popular skincare tool designed to massage the face, improve circulation, and help with lymphatic drainage to reduce puffiness.

Since it’s stainless steel, it’s naturally anti-bacterial and stays cool to the touch, which feels great on tired skin.

The Golden Rule: Use Oil or Serum

Never use this on dry skin. It will pull and irritate your face. Apply a facial oil, serum, or a thick moisturizer first so the tool glides smoothly.

How to Use It

Hold the tool at a 15 to 45-degree angle (almost flat against your skin) and use light to medium pressure. Always stroke upward and outward toward your hairline.

Part of FaceWhich Edge to UseMotion
JawlineThe curved "V" notchStart at the chin and glide along the jaw toward the earlobe.
CheeksThe long, flat sideStart at the side of the nose and sweep across the cheek toward the ear.
Under EyesThe small rounded endVery gently sweep from the inner corner out to the temple.
Brow BoneThe "V" notchFollow the curve of your eyebrow out toward the temple.
ForeheadThe long, flat sideStroke from the eyebrows up toward the hairline.

A Few Pro-Tips

  • Keep it Cold: Pop it in the fridge for 10 minutes before use to extra-depuff your face in the morning.
  • Wiggle at the End: When you reach the end of a stroke (near your ear or hairline), give it a little "massage wiggle" to help stimulate drainage.
  • Clean It: Since it’s metal, just wash it with warm water and a little mild soap after each use to keep it hygienic.
